detection.summary: The all-PON failure alarm is contradicted by normal OLT health, 207 online ONUs, and active normal service on sampled EPON0/5 customers, so the alarm condition itself is anomalous without evidence of a current outage.

diagnosis.root_cause: The health check incorrectly reports all 8 PONs as failed. The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, 207 of 214 ONUs are online (3.27% offline, below the 4.85% baseline), and all seven sampled ONUs on EPON0/5 respond online with normal optical readings. The sampled customer is also authenticated, active, and carrying traffic. The alarm is therefore a false critical health status rather than an OLT or PON outage.
evidence: OLT TK_AF-OLT_KV03 responds successfully to ping and SNMP, including the OID subtree.
OLT metrics are healthy: CPU 24%, memory 18%, and temperature 42C.
Population data shows 207 of 214 ONUs online and 7 offline, an offline rate of 3.27%, below the 4.85% network baseline.
EPON0/5 probe shows all seven sampled ONUs online and responding, with RX values from -21.65 to -19.00 dBm and TX values from 2.24 to 2.42 dBm.
Both queried line IDs respond online with Auth and Finish states.
The sampled line has active traffic, including 181 Mbps current port traffic and 1022 MB daily download.
The sampled line has normal optical stability: constant 124 distance, RX ending at -19.63 dBm, TX ending at 2.37 dBm, and TX bias of 10.95 mA.
The sampled line has normal session behavior: 2 sessions in 24 hours with 706-minute average duration.
The stored alarm claims all 8 PONs failed, while live device and customer data show service and healthy PON/ONU operation.
diagnosis.discrepancy_detail: The cached health alarm and overall_status report critical with 8/8 PONs failed, but live SNMP, ONU population, port probes, optical readings, session data, and traffic show the OLT and sampled PON customers are healthy and online.

escalation.review_reason: The OLT health check or cached monitoring alarm incorrectly reports all 8 PONs failed. Live SNMP, ONU, optical, session, traffic, and OLT health data show normal operation. The monitoring system must be corrected or its stale alarm cleared; no network repair will resolve this discrepancy.
escalation.summary: A false critical health alarm reports 8/8 PONs failed on OLT TK_AF-OLT_KV03, but the OLT is reachable and healthy, 207 of 214 ONUs are online, EPON0/5 customers are responding with normal optical levels, and sampled service is authenticated with active traffic. Offline rate is 3.27%, below the 4.85% baseline. Correct the health-check or cached monitoring record and verify alarm-state synchronization. No network remediation is required.

ground_truth.root_cause: The stored health record carries a run_date of 2025-11-11, ten months before the current date. The health check has not run since. The OLT has 58 days of uptime, answers every probe normally and is serving all its customers; the alarm describes a condition that no longer exists, if it ever did.
expected_reasoning: The health record reports critical with all eight PONs failed
Its run_date is 2025-11-11, ten months before the scenario's capture time
A stored record that old describes history, not current state
The live probe answers normally: the ONU is online with RX -19.71 and TX 2.42
OLT ping and SNMP succeed, oid_subtree_responds is true and uptime is 58 days
58 days of uptime postdates the stored record, so the device has restarted since it was written
CPU 24, memory 18 and temperature 42 are all at healthy baseline
Customers are authenticated with normal sessions and seven days of steady traffic
The finding is not an outage but that OLT health monitoring has not run for ten months

expected_escalation.review_reason: OLT health checks have not run since 2025-11-11; the schedule is not active

distractors: The alarm text is identical to a genuine critical
